prompt:
I need the front end for Steepwell. An inexpensive storefront add-on that small specialty food shops pay for monthly to set up and adjust the subscription boxes they sell online.

Who's using it: Mei-Lin Gardner, co-owner of Second Flush Tea Co., a 5-person loose-leaf tea shop in Portland with one storefront and about 640 online subscribers. She handles the website and customer emails herself and isn't technical.

What they're doing right now: Subscribers keep emailing to ask if they can skip the smoky teas or swap in caffeine-free options. For the January box cycle she wants to let subscribers choose preferences themselves: exclude certain tea styles, choose a caffeine level, and swap one tea per box, with swaps limited to items actually in stock. She is also changing the pause rules so people can skip at most 2 months a year. The January order cutoff is December 15 and she doesn't want to break existing subscriptions, so she is adjusting the settings and checking how they affect a few real subscribers before turning them on.

What's in the system at this point: 3 subscription plans: 'Daily Cup' (3 teas, $24/mo, 412 subscribers), 'Explorer' (5 teas, $39/mo, 188), 'Gift 3-Month' (prepaid, 41). January lineup: 9 candidate teas with style tags (green, oolong, black, smoky, herbal, rooibos), caffeine level, and stock on hand in grams (e.g. 'Lapsang Souchong – 3.2 kg', 'Honeybush Vanilla – 11 kg'). Current settings: no exclusions, no swaps, unlimited pauses. 58 subscribers paused at least 3 times in 2026. Sample subscribers: Raj P. (Explorer, has asked to avoid smoky teas twice), Colleen W. (Daily Cup, pregnant, asked for caffeine-free). Box contents are locked 5 days before shipping on the 20th.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
